text: If your menu is a PDF, people are leaving before they order.
Here's what happens on a phone. They tap Menu, and a file starts downloading.
It opens tiny. Pinch, zoom, scroll sideways, lose your place.
And it's often an old menu, because changing one price means making a whole new file.
If it's a scanned photo of the menu, screen readers can't read it at all.
So some customers can't even find out what you sell.
The fix? Put your menu on a normal web page.
Real text, big enough to read, with prices and tags like gluten free or vegan.
Now changing a price takes a minute, not a redesign.
Want a printable version? Keep the PDF as a small link at the bottom.
Open your own menu on your phone right now. Would you order from it? Follow for more website tips.
